title: Add a drain command that works the queue within a budget
summary: Add a CLI command (`drain`) that runs queued steward- and audience-queued requests itself: run, land and rate each item. It stops when the work's own check passes (for the explainer, the audience rates the live page 4 or more), when the user-set budget is spent, or when the same item fails twice (thrashing). It then reports where it stopped. The audience is the repository owner, who now runs go, land and rate by hand.

defaults_applied.how: Implemented in Rust in the athena-cli crate.
Fake-agent tests for each stop reason; clippy and fmt clean.
Verifier runs the tests and the --help output.
One command reusing existing run, land and rate paths.
No new crates; reuse existing orchestration.
The budget guard and the person-needed exclusion are enforced in code and pinned by tests.
Docs and CHANGELOG written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: An empty queue is not success: the loop reports 'queue empty, target not met' as a distinct stop reason.
The target is the audience rating threshold of 4 or more on the live page, read from the existing audience rating records; the threshold is a flag with default 4.
Thrashing means the same item fails (rejected or not landed) twice; the loop stops and names it.
Budget is a USD cap flag (and optional job-count limit); a job starts only if recorded spend plus its cap fits.
Items that need a person (above-ladder proposals) are listed as waiting and never accepted or landed by the loop.
Reuse existing run, land and rating functions in athena-core; the CLI only orchestrates.
No new config key; the choice is recorded in decisions.

acceptance_criteria.text: `cargo test` passes, with new fake-agent tests: (a) queue of two items, both run and landed, rating reaches 4+, stop reason 'target met'; (b) budget too small for the next job gives 'budget spent' with the remaining items still queued; (c) an empty queue with the target unmet stops at once with no spend and says the queue is empty, not success; (d) the same item failing twice gives 'repeated failure' naming the item.
`cargo run -p athena-cli -- drain --help` documents the budget, rating-threshold and job-limit flags and lists the stop reasons.
A unit test pins that no job starts when recorded spend plus the next job's cap would exceed the budget, including when an earlier job reported a cost above its estimate.

The final output (text and --json) names the stop reason, the jobs run with outcomes and costs, total spent, the latest rating against the target, and the items still queued or waiting for a person, so the owner can see where it stopped without opening records.
A test shows an item needing a person (above-ladder proposal) is listed as waiting and left untouched, never accepted, approved or landed by the loop.
README/docs and CHANGELOG describe the command, budget semantics, stop reasons, and what it does not decide; a decisions entry records the choice not to add a config key.

out_of_scope: Accepting, approving or landing items on a person's behalf
Changing the audience rating mechanism or the steward's proposal ladder
Adding a configuration key to athena.toml
departures: Larger than the reference: a new orchestrating command with several stop reasons, spanning run, land and rating paths, plus tests and docs.
